joya-de-nicaragua--cinco-de-cinco.description: Released in 2023 for Joya de Nicaragua's 55th anniversary, Cinco de Cinco is a soft-pressed blend of vintage Nicaraguan binder and filler under a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, rolled in Estelí. Earth and cocoa set the tone, joined by dark fruit, mineral notes and a pepper that grows as the body moves toward medium-full.

thirds.notes: Chocolate and dark fruit lead, with mineral earth and mixed pepper behind.
Mineral, earth and pepper build as the chocolate fades; pepper reaches the retrohale.
Pepper moves to the front with fruit and mineral, while chocolate and earth return underneath.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Cinco de Cinco
Cigar Coop – Joya de Nicaragua Cinco de Cinco Robusto Gordo review

joya-de-nicaragua--numero-uno.description: Número Uno began as a blend made for heads of state and handed out by Nicaraguan ambassadors on official missions; Joya de Nicaragua now places it in its Obras Maestras range. An Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler for a refined, creamy, medium-bodied smoke with a light thread of pepper.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Número Uno
Blind Man's Puff – Joya de Nicaragua Número Uno
Cigar Dojo – JDN Número Uno review

thirds.notes: Sweet and creamy, with cedar, salted peanut and browned butter, and cinnamon on the retrohale.
Gentle baking spices and cream, with florals, a vanilla-wafer sweetness and some orange zest.
Nuttiness leads, with cedar, soft spices and a floral thread to the finish.

joya-de-nicaragua--cinco-decadas.description: Named for five decades of Joya de Nicaragua, Cinco Décadas is rolled from extra-vintage leaves drawn from the factory's most exclusive tobacco reserves; the blend itself is kept confidential. It is silky, sweet and spicy, opening on earth and pepper and turning creamy and bread-like at the midpoint.

thirds.notes: Sweet earth with pepper and spice, settling into a deep, warming earthiness.
A creamy, bread-like sweetness takes over as the pepper and spice ease back.
The sweetness recedes while the rest of the profile holds steady to the end.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Cinco Décadas
Cigar Obsession – Joya de Nicaragua Cinco Décadas El General review

joya-de-nicaragua--cuatro-cinco.description: Cuatro Cinco marks 45 years of cigar making at Fábrica Joya de Nicaragua and first appeared as a limited edition in 2013. A Nicaraguan Habano Criollo wrapper and Dominican binder hold Grade A Nicaraguan filler, part of it rested in white-oak barrels. Spicy and robust, it shows espresso, red wood, orange peel and cayenne over a velvety finish.

thirds.notes: Early sweetness gives way to espresso and red wood, with bitter orange and cayenne.
Nuttiness comes and goes around a woody core as the cayenne grows stronger.
Wood and cream lead, at times with the orange note coming back.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Cuatro Cinco
halfwheel – Joya de Nicaragua Cuatro Cinco review

joya-de-nicaragua--antano-ct.description: Antaño CT sets a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper over the potent Nicaraguan binder and filler of the Antaño family, a deliberate contrast between a mild-looking leaf and a pungent core. The result is creamy yet assertive, with pronounced spice, at a medium-to-full pace that surprises anyone expecting a gentle Connecticut.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Antaño CT
Blind Man's Puff – Joya de Nicaragua Antaño CT Robusto

thirds.notes: Salted peanut, leather and coffee with dry grass, pepper on the retrohale and a creamy caramel sweetness.
Little change: dry grass, salted cashew and a steady sweetness.
Crisper and sharper, with a mineral brightness and roasted earth near the end.

joya-de-nicaragua--antano-dark-corojo.description: Antaño Dark Corojo is Joya de Nicaragua's power cigar: a Nicaraguan puro with a dark, oily, seal-brown Corojo Oscuro wrapper over mature, locally grown binder and filler. The blend is pungent and spicy, with an extra full body, yet it aims to stay smooth; a cigar for experienced smokers and a long evening.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Antaño Dark Corojo

joya-de-nicaragua--antano-1970-original.description: Antaño 1970 was introduced in 2001 by Dr. Alejandro Martínez Cuenca as a tribute to the Nicaraguan puro that Joya de Nicaragua sent to the United States in the 1970s. A Habano Criollo wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler; earth, leather, coffee and cocoa lead, with charred cedar building toward a bold, earthy finish.

thirds.notes: A sweet, creamy start of woody earth, leather, black coffee and cocoa, without pepper.
Balanced and woody, with leather, very dark chocolate and pleasant spice as the body rises.
Earthy and bold, with charred cedar and a touch of bitterness near the end.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Antaño Original
Famous Smoke Cigar Advisor – Joya de Nicaragua Antaño 1970 review

joya-de-nicaragua--antano-gran-reserva.description: Antaño Gran Reserva is a more mature take on the Antaño family: the richest, oiliest Nicaraguan Habano Criollo wrapper leaves over Nicaraguan binder and filler aged up to five years. Only extra-aged, selected tobacco goes into the blend, which keeps the line's full Nicaraguan character but presents it in a rounder, more refined form.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Antaño Gran Reserva

joya-de-nicaragua--joya-silver.description: Joya Silver is a box-pressed blend with an upper-priming Ecuadorian Habano oscuro wrapper, a Mexican San Andrés binder and Nicaraguan filler, part of the Joya family created by the company's younger team with its senior blenders. Medium in strength, it offers fresh spice with chocolate and a note of cherry.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Joya Silver
Cigar Inspector – Joya Silver Robusto
Blind Man's Puff – Joya de Nicaragua Silver Ultra

thirds.notes: Leather and gingerbread-like spice with cedar, a little citrus and salt, and a sweet chocolate note.
Pepper, wood and earth over leather, with cream and a brief floral, brown-sugar sweetness.
Cocoa and espresso with leather, toast and pepper, as the strength picks up.

joya-de-nicaragua--joya-cabinetta.description: Joya Cabinetta uses two wrappers on one cigar: Ecuadorian Connecticut along the body and a sun-grown Nicaraguan Habano Criollo at the head, over a mellower Nicaraguan binder and filler. The smoke is creamy and smooth, with pepper from the Criollo cap, a mild-to-medium choice for the daytime.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Joya Cabinetta

joya-de-nicaragua--joya-black.description: Joya Black follows Joya Red with a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, designed with the modern smoker in mind. It is medium-bodied but full of flavour, balanced and rich rather than forceful, for an evening when something darker than Joya Red is wanted.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Joya Black
Casas Fumando – Joya de Nicaragua Joya Black review
Kaplowitz – Joya Black cigar review

thirds.notes: Pepper and a meaty, yeasty note, with pencil-shaving cedar, dark chocolate and candied fruit.
Coffee and earth deepen, with hazelnut, hardwood and a brief raisin sweetness.
Hazelnut grows richer, the smoke turns creamier and a sweetness arrives at the end.

joya-de-nicaragua--joya-red.description: Introduced in 2014, Joya Red is a Nicaraguan puro with a claro Habano Criollo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler from Jalapa, Condega and Estelí. It starts smooth and creamy with light spice and vanilla, then builds nutty sweetness and a white-pepper bite; a medium-bodied everyday smoke.

thirds.notes: Smooth and creamy, with clean, light spice and a touch of vanilla.
A nougat-like sweetness appears and the spice sharpens into white pepper.
White pepper and cinnamon keep building, held in check by the tobacco's sweetness.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Joya Red
Cigar Dojo – Joya Red review

joya-de-nicaragua--rosalones-ct.description: Rosalones CT, the newest member of the Rosalones family, reverses the usual order: a Nicaraguan Habano Criollo Colorado wrapper over an Ecuadorian Connecticut binder and Nicaraguan filler. Woody with refined spice, it shows earth, pepper and coffee at a mild-to-medium strength, an everyday Nicaraguan in Robusto and Toro.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Rosalones CT

joya-de-nicaragua--rosalones-autenticos.description: Rosalones is one of the original Joya de Nicaragua brands, a smaller sibling of Clásico that returned at the end of 2010 after about two decades off the market. A Nicaraguan Habano Criollo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler gives a rich, medium-bodied smoke with steady, earthy flavour, made as a daily cigar.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Rosalones Auténticos
Blind Man's Puff – Joya de Nicaragua Rosalones 448 Consul

thirds.notes: Deep earth, black pepper and chocolate over a sweet tobacco base, with a faint oak note.
Bittersweet cocoa comes forward with background spice and a little bite.
Charred notes over coffee, a bittersweet chocolate finish and some wood.

joya-de-nicaragua--rosalones-reserva.description: Rosalones Reserva is a more selective version of the Rosalones blend, with a Nicaraguan Habano Criollo Colorado wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler chosen with greater care. Woody with refined spice and medium in strength, it comes in the RR sizes from the 444 to the 650.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Rosalones Reserva

joya-de-nicaragua--clasico-medio-siglo.description: Clásico Medio Siglo reworks Joya de Nicaragua's original best-selling cigar, first rolled more than fifty years ago, with a Nicaraguan Habano Criollo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It keeps the balance of the original while turning up the Nicaraguan character: wood, leather and spice at a medium body.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Clásico Medio Siglo

joya-de-nicaragua--clasico-original.description: Clásico is the house's original line, descended from the first cigar exported from Nicaragua and officially recognised as the country's national cigar; it is also Joya de Nicaragua's best seller in Europe. An Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler for a mild, woody and delicate smoke.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Clásico Original
Blind Man's Puff – Joya de Nicaragua Clásico Original Toro

thirds.notes: Dry cedar and oak with dried apricot, honey and walnut, and faint white pepper later.
Wood gives way to vanilla, baked bread and dried fruit, with cinnamon and a buttery finish.
Bright citrus with cashew, a light leather and white pepper in the background.

joya-de-nicaragua--flor-de-nicaragua.description: Flor de Nicaragua is one of Joya de Nicaragua's oldest brands, long sold only in northern Europe and now distributed worldwide, in a single Robusto. A claro Habano Criollo wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler gives a creamy, medium-bodied smoke of wood and leather, with lingering spice and dried fruit.

sources.title: Joya de Nicaragua – Flor de Nicaragua
